historical_timing_assessment.attempt_1: Swift exceeded 30m and was cancelled inside private Android binding. Generated consumer integration was skipped. This proves consumer-only extraction cannot remove the already observed failure path.
historical_timing_assessment.attempt_2: One Swift-only rerun succeeded in 1764 seconds (29m24s); the other three successful jobs were carried from attempt 1. 50 successful recorded Actions steps include setup/post steps and are not 50 source-defined check steps.
historical_timing_assessment.arithmetic_only: Removing the 654s moved chain from the prior 1764s job leaves 1110s (18m30s) including its observed non-step gaps. The new chain plus that run's checkout/probe/setup/post steps sums about 893s (14m53s), before any changed network, fresh-global-SwiftPM-cache or scheduling overhead. These are historical arithmetic, not new-job timings or an ETA.
historical_timing_assessment.current_snapshot_limit: Only retained ci-snapshot-5.json was inspected: run 40347513075 was in_progress at 2026-10-26T15:36:34Z, through archive completion with bridge active. This packet does not claim its final result or poll it.
historical_timing_assessment.verification_required: Run the actual changed workflow once after root integration and inspect all five terminal job conclusions plus retained artifacts. Any fresh failure must be classified from its own output; no automatic semantic pass or repeated retry is proposed.

alternatives.reason: Demonstrated cancellation occurred in the earlier binding step; prior successful consumer was only 150s. The core chain can hit the existing timeout before it reaches consumer.

alternatives.option: Extract only Android binding and rebuild its VM independently
alternatives.reason: Possible with fresh archive and exact source identity, but duplicates the archive build and leaves more accumulated work in the original job. The entire experimental chain is a cleaner single cut with existing fresh scratch paths.

alternatives.option: Capability archive upload/download across independent runners
alternatives.reason: Adds producer dependency, transport and a new custody validation surface. RUNNER_TEMP paths are runner-local; an exported receipt's absolute paths would be stale after download. A transport design must freeze source revision, target/architecture, tool identities, archive/header/source-manifest digests, regular-file/link/mode constraints, trusted artifact run/attempt identity and post-extraction custody, and validate all before bridge/activation consumers, which currently accept -I/-L without archive receipt admission. The binding runner's own digest checks are retained but cannot alone qualify all consumers. No handoff is needed for the proposed whole-chain cut.

alternatives.option: Move bridge modes to independent jobs
alternatives.reason: Each would need its own exact archive or a fully validated artifact transfer. Two macOS jobs already remove the measured accumulated path without dropping mode coverage.

limits_and_cleanup: Every existing source-defined workflow step and run payload is retained. New YAML validation is structural/data equivalence, not executed test coverage or GitHub schema/runner qualification.

Both macOS jobs retain timeout-minutes:30; existing step limits and production/runtime budgets are unchanged. A second runner increases possible aggregate CI job minutes and checkout/network work; no claim of reduced total compute is made.
No cache action, cross-runner path reuse, needs dependency, artifact download, continue-on-error, test filter change, retry, signing change or production budget increase is introduced.

Existing analyzer child-return/owned-scratch cleanup, capability builder process-group/cache-quarantine behavior and loopback listener/thread/temporary-key cleanup are unchanged. No new persistent local process or temporary native runtime is created by this review.

The binding runner still uses subprocess timeout semantics and reports ordinary host scenarios only; its Rust archive is not TSan-instrumented. Splitting jobs does not strengthen these existing limits or justify claiming device/JNI/Looper/signed UI/release/GA evidence.

All simulator/emulator runtime, physical phones, native UI, signing/store, separately published FieldLog, operational and GA gates remain pending according to AGENTS. Existing xcodebuild generic simulator compile is cross-compilation, not simulator runtime evidence.
